speaker: Doctor
text: Welcome to your consultation. I see you are experiencing agitation, yellowing of your skin and eyes, and abnormal lab results. To understand the underlying cause, please describe your recent alcohol consumption, any new medications, and whether you have noticed abdominal pain or changes in your urine or stool color.

speaker: Patient
text: 20-year-old male. The patient was previously healthy and has been brought to the emergency department due to agitation over the past 24 hours. Family members have noticed a yellowish coloring of his skin and eyes over the past week. The patient has a history of occasional cocaine and ecstasy use, and drinks alcohol socially on weekends. The patient also admits to high-risk sexual behaviors without using appropriate protection.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Viral Hepatitis (likely Hepatitis B or C) with acute liver injury.

The patient's history of high-risk sexual behavior combined with jaundice, agitation, and abnormal labs strongly suggests a viral etiology. Given his age and risk factors, I need to confirm this with specific serology. REQUEST TEST: Hepatitis Panel (HBsAg, Anti-HBc, Anti-HCV), Liver Function Tests (AST, ALT, Bilirubin, Alkaline Phosphatase), and Liver Ultrasound.
